page: Microsoft Azure E8bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EBDSv5 server family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes a 307 GB local SSD storage volume and supports Premium Storage configurations, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results position the E8bds_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory operations. The single-core Geekbench score is 1622.0, while the multi-core score reaches 6090.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 417.1 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 40.64 GB/sec. For database operations, the instance handles 7.99 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a Passmark database score of 4011.82. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium-sized 7B LLM inference tasks show weaker relative performance, with the 7B model processing prompts at 17.54 tokens per second and generating text at 7.83 tokens per second.

The E8bds_v5 offers a balanced qualitative cost profile for memory-intensive workloads that require moderate compute resources. The inclusion of 307 GB of local SSD storage and high memory density reduces the need for over-provisioning compute cores simply to acquire sufficient RAM. This makes the instance highly suitable for relational database hosting, caching layers, static web serving, and memory-bound enterprise applications. It is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded decompression or larger machine learning inference tasks that demand high-performance parallel processing.
